Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 2. Big happy family
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: I know you
- Materials: Family photos, question dice, interview sheet, COSYmanuals 'question words' and 'to be' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• ask Wh- questions about family members
• describe family relationships in detail
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles family vocabulary and possessives from Lessons 5–7.

Next lesson: Lesson 9 moves to objects and prepositions of place.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

who — a question word for a person. Example: Who is your teacher?
what — a question word for a thing. Example: What is your name?
how many — a question phrase for number. Example: How many brothers have you got?
where — a question word for a place. Example: Where do you live?
when — a question word for time. Example: When is your birthday?
why — a question word for a reason. Example: Why are you late?
family — parents, children, and relatives. Example: My family is big.
relative — a person in your family. Example: We visit our relatives at Eid.
close — near or emotionally connected. Example: We are a close family.
together — with each other. Example: We eat together every evening.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Who is this? (asking about a person)
• How many relatives have you got? (asking about family size)
• Where do they live? (asking about place)
• When do you visit them? (asking about time)
• Why are you close? (asking about a reason)
• Tell me about your family. (asking for a description)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.

Pronunciation Focus: Wh- question intonation and the /h/ sound in 'who'

who /huː/ — long /uː/
where /weə/ — starts with /w/
when /wen/ — short /e/
why /waɪ/ — long /aɪ/

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use question words to ask for different kinds of information.

Form:
Question words: Who (person), what (thing), where (place), when (time), why (reason), how (manner), how many (number). Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb.

Examples:
• Where are you from?
• Who is your teacher?
• How many brothers have you got?
• Why are you late?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___ are you from?
___ is your best friend?
___ many sisters have you got?
___ is your birthday?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• ___ is your teacher? (Who / Where / When)
• ___ do you live? (Where / Who / Why)
• ___ many people are in your family? (How / What / Who)
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What is your name?
• Where are you from?
• How many people are in your family?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three questions about your partner's family.
• Write three questions about your partner's home.
Reading: I know you

Tell me about your family. Who are they? How many relatives have you got? Where do they live? My family is big. I have many relatives. My grandparents live in a village, and my cousins live in the city. We are close and we spend holidays together. When do we meet? We meet every summer. Why? Because family is important.
Where do the grandparents live?
When does the family meet?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Who is that woman in the photo?
B: She is my aunt. She lives in Cairo.
A: How many cousins have you got?
B: I have five cousins.
A: When do you see them?
B: We meet every summer, and we are very close.
Where does the aunt live?
How many cousins does the speaker have?
Speaking task: Interview your partner about their family. Ask at least five Wh- questions and report two answers to the class.

• Who is the most important person in your family?
• How many relatives do you see every week?
• Where does your family usually meet?
• When do you spend time together?
• Why is family important in your culture?
Role-play: You are a journalist writing about family life. Interview a classmate and ask five Wh- questions about their family.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five Wh- questions about a friend's family, then write the answers.
Model: Who...? What...? Where...? When...? Why...?
